parts.title: Question 1
parts.q: A pattern has 6, 10, 14, 18 tiles. State how it changes each time, find the next term and find a rule using the position n.

parts.title: Question 2
parts.q: A number machine multiplies an input by 5 and then adds 2. The output is 47. Find the input, showing how you undo the steps.

parts.title: Question 3
parts.q: Solve 3x+8=35 and check your solution.

parts.title: Question 4
parts.q: Order 0.609, 0.69 and 0.069 from smallest to largest. Explain your place-value comparison.

parts.title: Question 5
parts.q: Calculate 32.4−8.76 and then multiply the result by 0.5. Show both stages.

parts.title: Question 6
parts.q: The travel times are 8, 10, 10, 12 and 15 minutes. Find the median, mean and range.

parts.title: Question 7
parts.q: Estimate 39.2×5.8 by rounding both values to 1 significant figure. Explain whether an exact answer of 227.36 is sensible.

parts.title: Question 8
parts.q: Convert 9/25 to a decimal and percentage, and give an equivalent fraction with denominator 100.

parts.title: Question 9
parts.q: At dawn the temperature is −5°C. It rises by 9°C, then falls by 6°C. Find the final temperature.

parts.title: Question 10
parts.q: A jumper costs £48. A sale reduces it by 25%. Find the discount and sale price.

parts.title: Question 1
parts.q: A rectangular garden is 7.5 m long and 4 m wide. Find its perimeter and area, with units.

parts.title: Question 2
parts.q: A triangle has base 14 cm and perpendicular height 5 cm. State the area formula and calculate its area.

parts.title: Question 3
parts.q: A bus departs at 23:48 and arrives at 00:27 the next day. Find the time taken in minutes and decimal hours.

parts.title: Question 4
parts.q: A cyclist covers 12 km in 40 minutes. Find average speed in km/h.

parts.title: Question 5
parts.q: On a distance–time graph, a straight section joins (4 s,6 m) to (10 s,30 m). Find the speed on that section.

parts.title: Question 6
parts.q: Write 42 and 70 as products of primes, then find their HCF.

parts.title: Question 7
parts.q: Two bells ring every 12 and 18 minutes. They ring together at 09:00. When will they next ring together?

parts.title: Question 8
parts.q: Calculate 3/4+5/6 and give a mixed number in simplest form.

parts.title: Question 9
parts.q: An isosceles triangle has a vertex angle of 44°. Find each base angle and explain your reasoning.

parts.title: Question 10
parts.q: A pictogram uses one symbol for 6 books. A group has 4½ symbols. Find its number of books and state why the key is essential.

parts.title: Question 1
parts.q: Share £150 in the ratio 2:3. Show the value of one ratio unit and both shares.

parts.title: Question 2
parts.q: A recipe for 4 people uses 300 g of rice. Find the rice for 10 people, using the same amount per person.

parts.title: Question 3
parts.q: A model uses scale 1:250. A wall is 4.8 cm on the model. Find its real length in metres.

parts.title: Question 4
parts.q: Expand and simplify 3(2x−5)+2(x+4).

parts.title: Question 5
parts.q: Find the equation of a line with gradient 2 through (3,8).

parts.title: Question 6
parts.q: Calculate 2/3÷5/6 and simplify.

parts.title: Question 7
parts.q: Reflect (5,−2) in x=1 and explain the distance check.
ms: Point is 4 units right of line

parts.title: Question 8
parts.q: A cuboid measures 12 cm by 5 cm by 4 cm and has mass 600 g. Find volume and density.

parts.title: Question 9
parts.q: Solve 5x−4<21 and state the largest integer that makes the inequality true.

parts.title: Question 10
parts.q: A £160 ticket rises in price by 12.5%. Find the new price using a multiplier.

parts.title: Question 1
parts.q: Values 1, 3 and 5 have frequencies 4, 2 and 4. Find the mean.

parts.title: Question 2
parts.q: A regular decagon has 10 sides. Find each exterior angle and each interior angle.

parts.title: Question 3
parts.q: A bag holds 6 red, 3 blue and 3 yellow counters. Find P(red), P(not red), and explain their sum.

parts.title: Question 4
parts.q: A club has 18 cyclists and 12 walkers. Of the cyclists, 7 wear a helmet in the survey category. A cyclist is selected. Find P(not in the helmet category).

parts.title: Question 5
parts.q: A circle has radius 7 cm. Give exact circumference and exact area, including units.

parts.title: Question 6
parts.q: A cylinder has radius 3 cm and height 5 cm. A cone has the same dimensions. Find both exact volumes.

parts.title: Question 7
parts.q: In a survey of 80 pupils, 30 walk to school. Find the walking sector angle in a pie chart.

parts.title: Question 8
parts.q: A scatter graph shows more revision time going with higher scores. State the correlation and two reasons this does not prove that extra revision caused the higher scores.
ms: Correlation alone does not prove revision time caused the difference

parts.title: Question 9
parts.q: After a 15% reduction a jacket costs £68. Find its original price.

parts.title: Question 10
parts.q: The sides of a triangle are given by x+2, x+3 and x+5 cm. Its perimeter is 31 cm. Find x and the longest side.

title: Year 9 · Practice paper A
coverage: Indices, roots and order of operations
Setting up, rearranging and solving equations

parts.title: Question 1
parts.q: Calculate 4.8÷0.16 and use multiplication to check your answer.

parts.title: Question 2
parts.q: Evaluate 16^(−1/2), explaining the root and reciprocal steps.

parts.title: Question 3
parts.q: Given 72=2³×3² and 120=2³×3×5, find their HCF and LCM.

parts.title: Question 4
parts.q: Calculate (8×10⁵)÷(2×10⁻²) and give the result in standard form.

parts.title: Question 5
parts.q: Simplify √75 and rationalise 5/√3.

parts.title: Question 6
parts.q: Expand (2x+3)(x−4) and collect like terms.

parts.title: Question 7
parts.q: Solve 4(x−2)=2x+10 and check your result.

parts.title: Question 8
parts.q: Make t the subject of v=u+at, stating a restriction on a.

parts.title: Question 9
parts.q: Solve −2<3x+1≤13 and give the integer solutions.

parts.title: Question 10
parts.q: Find the nth term of 4, 9, 16, 25 and use it to find the eighth term.

title: Year 9 · Practice paper B
coverage: Indices, roots and order of operations
Setting up, rearranging and solving equations

parts.title: Question 1
parts.q: Convert 0.454545… to a simplified fraction using algebra.

parts.title: Question 2
parts.q: £400 grows by 5% each year for two years. Find the final value and explain why adding 10% gives a different result.
ms: Second year uses the increased balance, so £440 from simple addition differs

parts.title: Question 3
parts.q: Red:blue=2:3 and blue:green=6:5. Find a single ratio red:blue:green.

parts.title: Question 4
parts.q: A right triangle has hypotenuse 17 cm and one shorter side 8 cm. Find the other side.

parts.title: Question 5
parts.q: A ladder has length 10 m and makes angle 30° with the ground. Find its vertical height and state the right-triangle ratio.

parts.title: Question 6
parts.q: A grouped class 20≤x<35 has frequency 24. Find its histogram frequency density and explain why class width matters.
ms: Frequency is proportional to bar area

parts.title: Question 7
parts.q: Explain interpolation and extrapolation on a scatter graph and state which normally has more support from the measured data.
ms: Interpolation normally has stronger support, since trend continuation outside is uncertain

parts.title: Question 8
parts.q: Velocity rises uniformly from 0 to 12 m/s in 5 s. Find acceleration and distance travelled.

parts.title: Question 9
parts.q: Find the equation of the line through (−1,1) and (3,9).

parts.title: Question 10
parts.q: For y=x²−16, find both x-intercepts and the y-intercept.

parts.title: Question 1
parts.q: A tile pattern has 4, 7, 10, 13 tiles. Give the next two terms and explain why the sequence is linear.

parts.title: Question 2
parts.q: A function machine multiplies by 4, then subtracts 1. Its output is 31. Find the input and check it.

parts.title: Question 3
parts.q: Four numbers have a mean of 7. Three numbers are 3, 6 and 9. Find the missing number.

parts.title: Question 4
parts.q: A composite bar shows 7 walkers and 5 cyclists on Monday. What total does the bar show? Explain how to draw dual bars for the same data.
ms: Dual bars would show separate heights of 7 and 5 for Monday.
Use a common scale and a key identifying walkers and cyclists.

parts.title: Question 5
parts.q: Write 2/5 as a decimal and percentage. Explain using an equivalent fraction with denominator 100.

parts.title: Question 6
parts.q: Calculate 3 − (−5). Explain using positive and negative counters or a number line.
ms: Subtracting −5 has the effect of adding 5.
A number line moves five steps right from 3; or add five zero pairs and remove five negative counters.

parts.title: Question 7
parts.q: Three eighths of a number is 27. Draw or describe an equal-part bar and find the whole.
ms: Three of eight equal parts represent 27.

parts.title: Question 8
parts.q: A 9 cm by 7 cm rectangle has a 3 cm by 2 cm corner removed. Find the remaining area, with units.
ms: The full rectangle has area 9 × 7 = 63 cm².
The removed corner has area 3 × 2 = 6 cm².

parts.title: Question 9
parts.q: A cyclist travels 6 km in 30 minutes. Convert the time to hours, then find the average speed in km/h.

parts.title: Question 10
parts.q: An isosceles triangle has a top angle of 44°. Find each of its two equal base angles, explaining the rules used.
ms: Triangle angles total 180°, so the two base angles total 136°.
The base angles are equal in an isosceles triangle.

parts.title: Question 1
parts.q: Red:blue = 2:5. There are 21 more blue counters than red. Find both amounts.
ms: The difference is 5 − 2 = 3 equal parts, so one part is 7.

parts.title: Question 2
parts.q: At the stated rate £1 = €1.25, convert €75 to pounds. Explain how a conversion graph would show this constant rate.
ms: A graph uses labelled pound and euro axes with even scales.
It is a straight line through the origin, including the point (£60, €75).

parts.title: Question 3
parts.q: Factorise 10x + 15 fully. Check by expanding and describe an equal-row tile arrangement.
ms: Five equal rows each contain two x-tiles and three unit tiles.

parts.title: Question 4
parts.q: A jacket costs £68 after a 15% reduction. Find the original price and check your result.
ms: £68 is 85% of the original, giving multiplier 0.85.

parts.title: Question 5
parts.q: A linear sequence is 4, 9, 14, 19, … Find its nth-term rule and its twentieth term.
ms: The common difference is 5, so start with 5n.

parts.title: Question 6
parts.q: A solid has mass 240 g and volume 80 cm³. State the density formula and calculate its density with units.

parts.title: Question 7
parts.q: Simplify a³ × a⁵ ÷ a² and state any restriction on a.
ms: a must not be zero because a² is a divisor.

parts.title: Question 8
parts.q: Of 40 pupils, 24 walk. Of the walkers, 16 carry a bag. Find the number who do not walk and the probability that a randomly selected walker carries a bag.
ms: The selected group has 24 walkers, not 40 pupils.

parts.title: Question 9
parts.q: A semicircle has radius 6 cm. Find its exact area and full perimeter.
ms: Full perimeter = 6π + 12 cm, including the diameter.

parts.title: Question 10
parts.q: Times are grouped into 0 ≤ t < 10 with frequency 4 and 10 ≤ t < 20 with frequency 6. Estimate the mean time and explain why it is an estimate.
ms: Use midpoints 5 and 15: the weighted total is 4 × 5 + 6 × 15 = 110.
Exact values inside the classes are unknown.

parts.title: Question 1
parts.q: Use prime factors to find the HCF and LCM of 18 and 30.
ms: All required prime powers give LCM = 2 × 3² × 5 = 90.

parts.title: Question 2
parts.q: £1000 earns 5% compound interest per year for two years. Find the final balance and explain why it is not £1100.
ms: The second year earns interest on the first year’s interest as well as on the original £1000.

parts.title: Question 3
parts.q: A closed cuboid is 2 cm by 3 cm by 7 cm. Find its surface area.
ms: The three face-pair areas are 6, 14 and 21 cm².

parts.title: Question 4
parts.q: Solve 3x + 7 = 5x − 9 and check the result.

parts.title: Question 5
parts.q: A tank starts with 20 litres. Water flows in at 9 litres/min and out at 4 litres/min. Find the volume after 6 minutes.

parts.title: Question 6
parts.q: An example £600 loan has 12 repayments of £56 and a separate £10 fee. Find the total repaid and the extra cost over the amount borrowed.
ms: Including the fee, the total repaid is £682.

parts.title: Question 7
parts.q: Describe a ruler-and-compasses construction of the perpendicular bisector of a 10 cm segment. Explain why the compass radius must exceed 5 cm.
ms: Draw equal-radius arcs above and below from both endpoints.
Join the two arc intersections; this line bisects the segment at 90°.
A radius greater than half the segment allows two distinct intersections.

parts.title: Question 8
parts.q: A Venn diagram has A only 4, both 3, B only 5 and neither 8. Find P(A ∪ B) and P(A ∩ B).
ms: The union contains 12, so P(A ∪ B) = 12/20 = 3/5.
The intersection contains 3, so P(A ∩ B) = 3/20.

parts.title: Question 9
parts.q: Find the y-intercept of y = 2ˣ. Explain why y = 1/x has no y-intercept.
ms: At x = 0, 2⁰ = 1, so the exponential graph crosses at (0,1).
1/0 is undefined, so the reciprocal graph has no point there.

parts.title: Question 10
parts.q: Enlarge point (3,2) by scale factor 2 from centre (1,1). Find the image and explain the movement from the centre.
ms: The original offset from the centre is (2,1).
Add the centre back: the image is (5,3).
